extracted.intended_audience: researchers and clinicians conducting or evaluating measurement reliability and instrument validation studies
extracted.subtask_description: Synthesizing and applying metrics and methodological practices for assessing inter-rater, intra-rater, and related measurement properties of observational instruments, checklists, and clinical scales across health and behavioral sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-rater reliability (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of agreement between different raters/observers when assessing the same subjects or samples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported across studies using multiple statistics (kappa, ICC, Krippendorff's alpha, etc.); can vary by item/category and may be improved by manuals, consensus training, or using multiple raters (average-measure ICC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intra-rater reliability (test-retest / consistency of same rater)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistency of a single rater's assessments across repeated measurements or presentations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed by repeating cases (same rater presented the same case multiple times) and computing ICCs or other agreement measures (e.g., studies reported excellent intra-rater ICCs and used repeated presentations to estimate consistency).

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which items on a multi-item instrument measure the same construct (e.g., Cronbach's alpha).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess checklist/scale homogeneity; example: Cronbach's alpha reported alongside kappa for a checklist and low alpha suggested limited internal consistency despite substantial IRR. Use with caution—alpha reflects item intercorrelation, not interrater agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test-retest reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Stability of instrument scores over time when no true change is expected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed by having participants complete the instrument twice (e.g., survey completed twice to assess test-retest reliability); often reported with intraclass correlation coefficients or weighted kappa for ordinal items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reliability coefficient for continuous or ordinal measures reflecting consistency or absolute agreement among raters (various ICC models, e.g., ICC(2,1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used widely for percent measures, continuous scores, and average-measure reliability; studies report single-measure and average-measure ICCs and use thresholds (e.g., ≥0.70 as acceptable). Report model and type (consistency vs absolute agreement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohen's kappa (unweighted) and weighted kappa
rubrics_metrics.description: Chance-corrected agreement statistic for categorical ratings; weighted versions account for ordinal distance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used at item-level for categorical/ordinal scales; both unweighted and weighted kappa values were reported (e.g., unweighted Cohen's kappa for item-level agreement; weighted kappa for ordinal Raymond Scale). Fine-tune manuals to improve kappa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Light's kappa
rubrics_metrics.description: A multi-rater generalization of Cohen's kappa used to assess agreement among more than two raters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to trichotomous checklist data with three raters (example: overall IRR 0.70 using Light's kappa).

rubrics_metrics.name: Krippendorff's alpha
rubrics_metrics.description: A reliability coefficient suitable for multiple raters and various data types (nominal, ordinal, interval).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess inter-rater agreement across many raters (example: Krippendorff's alpha ranged 0.15–0.45 for rat detection across animals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Yule's Q
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure of association used here to assess intra-rater reliability for binary detection outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to repeated binary classification by the same rater (example: mean Yule's Q = 0.9 indicating high intra-rater reliability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentage absolute agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportion of exact agreement between raters on scale components or items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported alongside ICCs and kappas to show item-level agreement ranges (e.g., 31%–92%). Useful to identify specific items with low absolute agreement even when summary statistics are acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard error of measurement (SEM) and minimum detectable change (MDC)
rubrics_metrics.description: SEM quantifies score precision; MDC is the smallest change beyond measurement error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computed from reliability data to interpret individual score changes (example: SEM and MDC reported for Anteromedial Reach Test; MDC and ±error used to interpret clinical significance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Area under the ROC curve (AUC) / prognostic accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Discrimination metric for prognostic instruments, comparing predicted outcome accuracy (AUC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compare abbreviated vs full scales (example: a 3-item abbreviated NIHSS retained AUC ~0.90 compared with full NIHSS). Pair with reliability estimates to balance brevity, accuracy, and reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Bland & Altman plots and Pearson correlation
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods to assess agreement between instruments/scales (Bland & Altman) and association between total scores (Pearson r).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied when comparing two instruments (example: comparing OPTION-12 and OPTION-5: Pearson r and Bland & Altman used; systematic differences noted). Use Bland & Altman to detect systematic bias even when correlation is high.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity and specificity estimation using Bayesian methods from interrater reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Using known interrater agreement (e.g., kappas) to form priors on sensitivity/specificity to correct misclassification bias in effect estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrated by Bayesian correction of odds ratios when exposure is assessed by experts: translate kappa-based interrater reliability into priors on sensitivity/specificity to adjust effect estimates and credible intervals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighted kappa coefficients and standard cut-offs for acceptable reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of thresholds (e.g., ICC or kappa ≥0.70) to judge acceptable reliability for translated/implemented instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: interRAI LTCF items — 197/198 items met or exceeded standard cut-offs for acceptable test-retest and inter-rater reliability after translation. Specify and justify thresholds appropriate to the instrument and use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content validity via expert consensus/Delphi
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishing instrument items and content relevance using literature review and iterative expert consensus (Delphi rounds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: checklist developed via literature review and three rounds of Delphi with six experts; supports content validity and grounds items prior to psychometric testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring format design (e.g., trichotomous done/not done/not applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Choice of item response categories and scoring rules affects reliability and usability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a 24-item checklist used trichotomous scoring (done / not done / not applicable) for observed behaviors; document scoring rules clearly and train raters on how to apply categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manualization and standardized rater training / consensus training
rubrics_metrics.description: Creating measurement manuals with clear item definitions and conducting standardized rater education to improve interrater reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple studies recommend manuals and training; one study found fine-tuning manuals and consensus training improved kappa (OPTION instruments) and consensus training reduced diagnostic variation among faculty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using multiple raters and reporting average-measure reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculating average-measure ICCs (or multi-rater statistics) to reflect reliability when multiple raters will be used in practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: average-measure ICC for four raters yielded strong inter-rater agreement for many QUALIDEM subscales even when single-measure ICCs were lower. Report both single- and average-measure coefficients relevant to intended use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting variables via data reduction (e.g., principal component analysis) to improve reliability and brevity
rubrics_metrics.description: Using PCA or similar methods to identify most prognostically relevant components and create abbreviated instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: abbreviated NIHSS derived from PCs retained high prognostic accuracy and had improved estimated interrater reliability; validate abbreviated instruments in independent cohorts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure patterning (proportions) vs raw counts for observational data
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparing reliability of proportional/patterning indicators versus raw counts when coding behaviors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studies found patterning (proportional indicators) often produced higher inter-rater reliability and better predictive validity than raw counts; empirically compare both approaches rather than choose a priori.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare ordinal classification vs continuous percent measures for reporting (e.g., Raymond Scale vs percent embolization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Choice of reporting format (categorical ordinal scale vs continuous percent) can affect interrater reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: percent embolization (continuous) showed better inter- and intra-rater agreement (ICC) than Raymond ordinal scale (kappa); consider continuous measures where feasible to improve concordance.
